chunks: Voltage divider: draw, equation, derivation. The question: Draw a voltage divider circuit. What is the voltage divider equation? Derive it.
A voltage divider is two resistors in a row that turn a bigger voltage into a smaller one.
You connect the big voltage across both resistors and take your output from the point between them.
The output is a fixed fraction of the input, and the two resistor values set that fraction.
Think of a staircase that drops 9 meters from top to bottom. If you stop at a landing partway down, you have only dropped part of the height.
Two equal flights put the landing at half height. A short flight on top and a long flight below put the landing high up.
Voltage "drops" across resistors the same way height drops across flights of stairs: the bigger resistor takes the bigger share of the drop.
The output is the voltage across R₂ , measured from the middle node to ground. With nothing attached at V out, the same current I flows through both resistors.
Voltage (V): the electrical "push", measured between two points. Like height difference on the staircase. Current (I): how much charge flows per second, measured in amps.
Like how many people walk down the stairs per second. Resistance (R): how hard a part makes it for current to flow, measured in ohms (Ω). Ohm's law: V equals I times R .
The voltage across a resistor equals the current through it times its resistance. In series: connected end to end, so the same current must pass through both.
Ground: the point we call 0 volts and measure everything else from.
Put 10 volts across two equal 1 kilohms resistors in series. The same current flows through both, and they are identical, so each one drops the same voltage: 5 volts each.
The point between them sits at 5 volts , half the input. Now make the bottom resistor 3 kilohms and keep the top one at 1 kilohms.
The bottom resistor is 3 parts out of 4 total, so it gets 3/4 of the voltage: the middle point sits at 7. 5 volts .
That is the whole idea: the output is the input multiplied by "bottom resistor over total resistance".
"A voltage divider is two resistors in series across V in , with the output taken across the bottom one: V out equals V in R 2 over (R 1 plus R 2) .
It comes straight from series current: I equals V in over (R 1 plus R 2) , and V out equals IR 2 . The key caveat is that it assumes no load current.
A load appears in parallel with R 2 and pulls the output down, so dividers are for setting references and scaling signals, not for powering things."
